How to sign a PDF online for free

Open Sign, draw your signature with a finger or mouse, tap the page where it goes, and press Place the signature.

Sign →Free. Nothing is uploaded.

How to do it

  1. Open Sign and add the PDF.
  2. Draw your signature in the box, or type your name instead.
  3. Tap the page where the signature goes.
  4. Drag it to move it, and drag its corner to resize it.
  5. Press Place the signature and save the signed PDF.

More than one place

Agreements often need a signature on every page. Go to the next page and tap again: the same signature goes down each time. To write the date or your name beside it, use Add text. For a form with real fields, fill it in first with Fill in a form.

Using your signature on paper

If you would rather use your real ink signature, sign a sheet of white paper, photograph it, and place the photo with Add image. A PNG with a see-through background sits cleanly on the page.

A drawn signature and a digital one

A drawn signature is a picture of your handwriting on the page. That is what most everyday forms, rental agreements and office paperwork expect. It does not prove who placed it. When a document must carry a certificate that a reader can check, such as with a Class 3 DSC, you need a digital signature instead.

Questions people ask

Is my signature saved anywhere?

No. It is drawn in your browser, placed on your PDF, and forgotten when you leave the page. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

Can I sign on my phone?

Yes. Draw with your finger; the page and the pad are made for touch.

Is a drawn signature legally valid?

Whether it is accepted depends on the document and who receives it. Many everyday documents accept one; some legal and government filings require a certificate-based digital signature.

Your file stays on your device. Foolscap does the work inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded and there is nothing for anyone to keep. How you can check
